newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen falling at open, tracking bonds.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen falling at open, tracking bonds.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to slide at the open on Friday, mirroring a sharp fall in bond prices which pointed to a higher interest rate outlook.
Analysts said the Dow industrials could shed anywhere from 50 to 100 points shortly after the open, as the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond lost 18/32 to yield 6.57 percent.

"Long-term rates have risen above 6.50 percent, which has brought jitters to the bond market and should take its toll on the stock market," Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments, said. Cardillo said stocks could fall 70 to 110 points at the open, based on futures.
In early trade, the Standard & Poor's 500 futures index sank 10 points to 946.25.
Treasury prices, whose slide yesterday sparked profit-taking in the stock market, extended losses amid deteriorated technical conditions.

"The weakness in the bond market without any real hard news is disquieting," Arnold Kaufman, editor of Standard & Poor's Outlook investment advisory news letter, said. He said the Dow could drop 50 points after the open.
In London, the FTSE-100 stock index also tumbled as U.S. Treasury prices fell. It was off 71.1 at 5015.7.

Bond prices started their downturn on Thursday, after the U.S. Treasury released results from its $10 billion auction of 30-year bonds, the final leg in its quarterly refunding operation. A rise in yields triggered profit-taking in stocks, and the Dow closed down 71 points at 8188.
"The stock market cannot continue to go up without a stable bond market," Cardillo said.

Analysts said the stock market was vulnerable to a pull-back after its robust gains this year. They also said markets would watch for any signs of weakness in the recently-strong dollar, which could hurt bonds and stocks.
